steps.description: Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 5 samples (the smallest group size). Do not scale, transform or normalize the counts beforehand — DESeq2 estimates median-of-ratios size factors and applies them as offsets inside the negative binomial model. Coerce subject and condition to factors, set the control level of condition explicitly as the reference (do not rely on alphabetical ordering), fit design ~ subject + condition, and run the Wald test on the condition coefficient, naming the contrast as (factor=condition, numerator=treated, denominator=control) so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Extract results with alpha=0.05 and independent filtering left on, BH adjustment. Shrink the condition coefficient with apeglm and keep the unshrunken log2FC in the same table. Report the number of genes tested after filtering, the number with padj<0.05, and — separately — the number of genes whose p-value is NA because of the Cook's-distance count-outlier flag versus NA from independent filtering; at 5 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers. Write the full results table (all tested genes) and the significant subset as CSV.

plan.title: Paired treated vs control blood RNA-seq DE + GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer count matrix (/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 11 columns — one gene-symbol column plus 10 sample columns) from STAR/featureCounts, with a 10-row sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv: sample, subject, condition) describing 5 human blood donors each contributing one control and one treated sample. The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is exactly a paired two-group contrast, so the whole plan is built around a within-subject design rather than a between-group comparison.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any test: library sizes, blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes and a Euclidean sample-distance heatmap, coloured by condition and by subject. With n=5 pairs the dominant expected structure is subject identity, and the QC must state whether samples pair up by subject and whether any of the 10 samples departs from its pair — that determines whether the blocking term is doing what it should. T1S2 is the core test: pre-filter minimally (>=10 counts in at least 5 samples, the smallest group size), let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model (counts are never pre-scaled), fit ~ subject + condition with the control level set explicitly as the reference, and take the Wald test on the condition coefficient. The subject term absorbs between-donor variation, so the reported effect is the within-subject treatment response the question asks for. Fold changes are shrunk with apeglm on that coefficient, the unshrunken estimate is kept alongside, and selection is by BH-adjusted p-value at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. At 5 pairs DESeq2 flags Cook's-distance count outliers and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing counts, so the step reports outlier-NA genes separately from independent-filter NAs. T1S3 is a robustness check: the same counts, the same paired design, tested with edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test; the intersection with the DESeq2 calls is the high-confidence set and method-unique genes are listed separately, since the two tools disagree most at low replicate numbers — which is where this dataset sits.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes (ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — the disputed choice under R-0007, chosen because it is signed and standard-error-scaled and does not need a second shrinkage pass) and runs preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark for human, sets restricted to 15-500 genes after intersecting with the tested universe, BH-adjusted, redundant sets collapsed. No reference store is provisioned in this environment right now, so this step must first resolve a human hallmark gene-set collection from whatever the environment holds and, if none is available and no package can supply one, report that plainly and stop rather than substituting a different organism's sets or an arbitrary collection — enrichment is an annotation layer on top of the DE result, not the answer to the research question, so its loss costs one step and not the run. T2S2 assembles the report: design formula, contrast direction, thresholds, package versions, n tested and n DE, the two-method overlap, and the enrichment provenance (database, version, rank metric, universe, size window) with the caveat that enrichment results are method-dependent.

Two honest limits are carried through: 5 pairs is small, so power is modest and effect-size estimates for low-count genes are unreliable even after shrinkage; and the package inventory for this environment could not be read, so every step must probe its libraries (requireNamespace / import) before use and fail with a clear message rather than a stack trace.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library sizes
Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 5 samples
Paired design ~ subject + condition with explicit reference level control
DESeq2 Wald test with design ~ subject + condition
apeglm log fold change shrinkage on the condition coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate with independent filtering
fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic with MSigDB Hallmark
Reproducibility report: method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, DESeq2 vs edgeR QL overlap, session info
